summary: This lecture tells of the 12-year-old Prophet SAW's journey to Sham with Abu Talib. The ustaz introduces Abu Talib's family and his wife Fatimah bint Asad, then explains the hardship of crossing the desert by camel and by the stars. At Busra, the monk Bahira saw a cloud and a tree shading the caravan, invited them to a meal and recognised the Prophet SAW from the signs in his books. He advised Abu Talib to take him back to Mecca. The ustaz also notes that some sirah researchers doubt this event, and closes with two stories of how Allah protected him as a youth from bad entertainment and from uncovering himself.
keyPoints: Abu Talib, whose real name was Abdul Manaf, had six children and his wife Fatimah bint Asad cared for the Prophet SAW like a mother.
At 12 the Prophet SAW pleaded and was finally allowed to go with Abu Talib on a trading trip to Sham.
At Busra, the monk Bahira saw a cloud shade the caravan and a tree lower its branches, and recognised him as the final prophet.
Bahira advised Abu Talib to take him home because he feared people in Sham would harm him.
Allah protected him from bad entertainment and from uncovering himself from childhood.

chapters.title: Opening
chapters.summary: The ustaz continues the sirah after the pupils finish presentations about the body.

chapters.title: Abu Talib's family
chapters.summary: Abu Talib's real name was Abdul Manaf. He had six children and his wife Fatimah bint Asad cared for the Prophet SAW like a mother.

chapters.title: Abu Talib's trade and the Prophet's wish
chapters.summary: Abu Talib traded to Sham in summer and Yemen in winter. The Prophet SAW, who would miss him, wanted to come.

chapters.title: Abu Talib gives in
chapters.summary: Abu Talib said no, but out of love he finally let the Prophet SAW come.

chapters.title: Crossing the desert
chapters.summary: There is no road in the desert. They covered their faces from sand, travelled at night guided by stars, and took turns on watch because of dangerous animals.

chapters.title: Busra and the monk Bahira
chapters.summary: The caravan stopped at Busra, where a scholar named Bahira read many old books.

chapters.title: The cloud and the tree
chapters.summary: Bahira saw a cloud shading the caravan and the tree giving more shade to those sitting under it.

chapters.title: The invitation to a meal
chapters.summary: Bahira invited everyone to eat, which he had never done, and found that a boy had been left minding the goods.

chapters.title: The scriptures foretell the final prophet
chapters.summary: Jews and Christians knew from their books that a prophet named Ahmad would come, and the signs were present.

chapters.title: Bahira asks about his father
chapters.summary: Bahira said the boy must have no father, so Abu Talib admitted he was his uncle.

chapters.title: The warning and the sign of prophethood
chapters.summary: Bahira advised Abu Talib not to take him to Sham and pointed to a sign the size of a quail's egg on his back.

chapters.title: The view of sirah researchers
chapters.summary: Some researchers doubt it because Abu Talib later did not embrace Islam, if he really knew.

chapters.title: Protected from entertainment
chapters.summary: When he wanted to hear singing at a wedding, he fell asleep two nights in a row.

chapters.title: Protected from uncovering himself
chapters.summary: When children carried stones without their cloths, he was knocked down and told not to remove his cloth.

chapters.title: Closing and Fatimah bint Asad
chapters.summary: He is now 15. Fatimah bint Asad later embraced Islam and he called her mother.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions Allah asking whether they do not look at how the camel was created, when explaining the camel's eyes that shield from sand.
dalil.translation: Do the disbelievers not see how rain clouds are formed
A monk named Bahira recognised the Prophet SAW from the signs in his book and hid him from seven men who were looking for him.
dalil.context: The ustaz says a hadith mentions seven soldiers coming to look for him. He does not name a narrator or source.

books.context: A summary of the sirah covering the journey to Sham and Bahira.

people.role: Abu Talib's wife and foster mother of the Prophet SAW
people.context: Cared for the Prophet SAW like a mother, later embraced Islam, migrated to Madinah and was shrouded by him personally.
Brought the Prophet SAW home to his grandfather after Aminah died.
Mentioned as someone who went trading and never returned, dying in Gaza.
Read old scriptures, recognised the signs of prophethood and advised Abu Talib to take him home.
Mentioned for the Torah, which speaks of the coming of the final prophet.
Told that after him a prophet named Ahmad would come.

sirah.era: The Prophet's youth: the journey to Sham
sirah.summary: This lecture covers the Prophet's journey to Sham at 12, the meeting with Bahira and Allah's protection of him until 15.

events.title: The Prophet SAW lives in Abu Talib's house
events.desc: After his grandfather died, he moved to Abu Talib's house, a large family.

events.label: Sham
events.title: Going with Abu Talib to Sham
events.desc: Abu Talib relented and let him come.

events.label: Cloud
events.title: A cloud shades the caravan
events.desc: Bahira saw a cloud following and shading the caravan.

events.label: Meal
events.title: Bahira invites them to eat
events.desc: Bahira invited everyone to eat and found a boy had been left behind.

events.label: Recognised
events.title: Bahira recognises him
events.desc: Bahira said this is the one he had been looking for.

events.label: Warning

events.desc: Bahira advised Abu Talib not to take him to Sham.

events.label: Singing

events.label: Modesty

events.desc: He fell and heard a voice forbidding him to remove his cloth.

lessons.title: Allah protects whom He wills
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW fell asleep when he wanted to hear singing, because Allah guarded him from what harms the heart and character.

lessons.title: Modesty and covering oneself
lessons.body: He was forbidden from removing his cloth even as a child, so we too must keep modesty.

lessons.title: Lowering the gaze
lessons.body: When we see improper pictures in magazines or shopping malls, we close or change them.

lessons.title: Abu Talib's affection
lessons.body: Abu Talib softened and let the Prophet SAW come because he loved him so much.

lessons.title: Reflecting on Allah's creation
lessons.body: The camel has lashes like wipers that protect its eyes, a sign of Allah's creation.

lessons.title: Knowledge reveals the signs of truth
lessons.body: Bahira recognised the signs because he read his scriptures.

lessons.title: The Prophet SAW was always looked after
lessons.body: Although he had no father or mother, he was cared for by his grandfather, Ummu Aiman and Abu Talib.

lessons.title: Differing views on the sirah
lessons.body: Some researchers doubt the Bahira story because Abu Talib did not embrace Islam.

lessons.title: A foster mother who cared
lessons.body: Fatimah bint Asad cared for him like a mother and later embraced Islam.
